title: Compact scope hierarchy and curated permissions matrix for RBAC v2
creator: Avery Chen
description: Context: RBAC v1 served us well for early adopters but lacks expressivity for: multi-tenant resource shapes, fine-grained admin controls, cross-tenant delegated roles, and consistent auditability required by regulated customers. Goal: produce a compact, auditable role model (RBAC v2) that maps cleanly to Redwood resource hierarchy, supports scoped role grants, makes permission evaluation deterministic, and integrates with audit logging and SSO/SAML role mapping. The design must minimize token size for request-time evaluation, support efficient caching of grants, and allow safe default-deny behavior for new actions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented resource hierarchy with canonical scope identifiers (org, project, pool, model) and example URNs. 2) Permissions matrix that covers ~95% of observed actions from the last 12 months of audit logs with categorical labels (read/write/admin/audit). 3) Deterministic evaluation rules (ordering + overrides) documented with examples. 4) End-to-end test harness and a sample migration script to translate RBAC v1 role bindings into RBAC v2 suggestions for customers. 5) Security review sign-off and a small perf benchmark showing no more than 8% added latency for token evaluation on p99 path.
design_decisions: Use canonical resource URNs prefixed: r:org:<org_id>, r:proj:<proj_id>, r:pool:<pool_id>, r:model:<model_id> to simplify caching and wildcard scopes.
Adopt a compact grant representation: [subject, scope, permission-set, grant-id, when, expires] to reduce evaluation cost and network size.
Evaluation policy: explicit deny > explicit allow > inherited allow > default deny. This provides safest behavior for admin/scoped deny use-cases.
Support both role-based grants (role -> permission set) and direct permission grants for bootstrap/admins to ease migration.
Map SAML/SSO attributes to 'role assertions' at login time and persist as claims; implement short-lived session binding so role changes in IdP take effect within 10 minutes via refresh.
Audit hooks: every grant evaluation must emit a structured audit event with grant_id, evaluation_reason, resolution, and policy_version to the audit pipeline.
To avoid permission explosion, include aliases/grouping for common permission sets (e.g., "billing-admin" => [billing:read, billing:write, invoices:issue]).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design + proto): finalise URN schema, permission taxonomy and evaluation doc (owner: Jordan) — 2 weeks. Phase 2 (runtime): add grant evaluator that consumes compact grants and returns verdict + audit event; integrate with existing auth middleware (owner: infra-auth team) — 3 weeks. Phase 3 (console + migration): UI for role creation and a migration CLI to propose role conversions from RBAC v1 (owner: console+tools) — 3 weeks. Phase 4 (QA + perf + security review): run benchmarks, fuzz tests, and threat modelling; fix issues and cut release candidate — 2 weeks.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: permission model complexity grows and confuses customers -> mitigate by providing curated starter roles and UI presets. Risk: policy evaluation adds latency -> mitigate with in-memory caching keyed by user+scope and precomputed effective-grants for high-volume service accounts. Risk: stale SSO assertions -> mitigate by short-lived session claims and proactive refresh endpoints. Risk: audit volume increases -> mitigate by sampling non-critical evaluations and ensuring logs can be filtered and aggregated efficiently.
updates: 2025-02-14: Created ticket and initial draft of permission taxonomy. Linked prototype evaluator PR for early feedback.
2025-02-20: Review with security & infra. Decided on explicit deny precedence and compact grant encoding. Action: Aaron (infra) to validate cache eviction semantics.
2025-02-24: UX sync — console team requested role aliasing and CSV import for large orgs. Added to Phase 3 scope.
2025-02-28: Discovered dependency (ENG-49900) which adds attribute-based indexing to document DB; blocked until schema change lands. Marked dependency.
2025-03-03: Added audit event schema and example events. Security review queued for 2025-03-10.
2025-03-03: Performance micro-benchmarks of prototype evaluator: median added latency 0.9ms, p99 added latency 6.2ms in bench harness (caveat: prototype not using production cache).
review_feedback: Security (Maya R.): include correlation_id in audit events and require KMS-wrapped log signatures for tenant-sensitive events.
Product (Liam S.): provide migration UX that surfaces 'dangerous' permission mapping where RBAC v1 implicit grants map to RBAC v2 allow+no-deny.
Infra (Aaron K.): ensure grant cache has TTL aligned with SSO refresh window and support forced invalidation via control-plane webhook.
open_questions: Do we allow 'scoped deny' to be granted at lower-level resources (e.g., deny model-delete at project scope while allowing at org scope)? What should be the admin UX for overrides?
What is the serialization size budget for a single user's effective-grants claim in JWTs for mobile clients? (target < 2kb)
How do we handle external app tokens that need only signing rights (i.e., narrow permission sets) without becoming service accounts?
migration_plan_notes: The migration CLI will read RBAC v1 bindings, surface likely equivalent RBAC v2 suggestions grouped by org, and flag ambiguous mappings where implicit inheritance was used. Provide an "apply-safely" mode that creates 'suggested' roles and binds them to a sandbox org for customer verification before switching production.
qa_and_test_cases: 1) unit tests for evaluation precedence with nested scopes and explicit denies. 2) integration test with SAML role assertions and refresh flow. 3) audit-log verification: ensure every evaluation writes the correct structured event. 4) migration round-trip test (v1 -> v2 -> v1-simulated-check) to validate behavior parity where intended.
estimated_rollout: Beta: opt-in for 10 pilot customers (platform-2025.04-beta); GA: platform-2025.06. Rollout plan includes opt-in, monitoring of error rates and permission regression alerts, and a rollback path to RBAC v1 bindings per-org.
final_notes: This ticket focuses on the core role model and evaluation semantics; follow-up tickets will address RBAC UI polish, tenant-admin analytics, and cross-tenant delegations. Please leave design comments in the Confluence doc and tag @Avery for clarifications.
